newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds gain late, eye on Brazil deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds gain late, eye on Brazil deal.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Monday after a late spurt of short-covering ahead of Brazil's 30-year global bond offering Tuesday.
"There were some shorts on the day. It was speculation ahead of the Brazil deal," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/4 at 93-1/2 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.15 to 123.60.
The market traded slowly earlier in the session and was only boosted late, mainly by foreigners, said the trader.

The Brazilian swap deal allows investors to switch their Brazilian Par and Cs bonds for the new 30-year issue. The deal is expected to range from a minimum $1 billion to about $4 billion. Results will be announced Wednesday.

Apart for investors hopefully eying the Brazilian market, traders said the market was looking healthy, with last week's acquisitions by foreign banks of local ones underpinning the optimism around Argentina's economy.
"The tendency continues to be upward," said another trader.
Call money rates fell to 5.78 percent from 5.98 percent.
